messages.subject: Multi-group SEM with lavvan
parts:
Hello all,

I'm trying to do multigroup SEM with lavaan. I figured out how to do it with raw data, but want to know whether I can also do this process with correlation (or covariance) matrix. I googled about it, and found that there is a way to input correlation matrix for sem but cannot find combination of multigroup SEM.

I know it can be done in lisrel, is it possible to do this in R? I hope somebody gives me helpful advice!

Many Thanks!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Multi-group SEM with lavvan
parts: if I want to use correlation instead of covariance, I put a correlation matrix? Is there any function instead of sample.cov (i.e. sample.cor)?

No, this is Covariance Structure Analysis.  Correlations have variances fixed to 1, so fitting a model to a correlation matrix is only going to return correct SEs and test statistics if you constrain residual variances to = 1 - explained variance.  

http://www.statpower.net/Content/319SEM/Reading/Cudeck89.pdf

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Multi-group SEM with lavvan
parts: what should I do for the syntax?

If you have access to the covariance matrix, analyze that.  You can request a standardized solution to see things in a standardized metric:

http://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/sem.html

If you have the correlation matrix and SDs, you can transform the correlation into a covariance matrix using cor2cov() function

?cor2cov

If you only have the correlation matrix, I would have to see your model to show you an example of how to apply the appropriate constraints to get SEs you can trust.

Terrence D. Jorgensen

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Multi-group SEM with lavvan
parts: what should I do for the syntax?

Since you posted your model syntax in another thread, I'll follow-up here.  I label your parameters using "b" for beta (regression slopes) and "p" for psi (covariance matrix of disturbances).  It helps if you can find a text explaining covariance algebra and/or path-tracing rules, like Loelin's (2004) Latent Variable Models (4th ed.) or Bollen's (1989) Structural Equations with Latent Variables.  You can ask around on SEMNET for resources to learn path-tracing rules and covariance algebra.

Model <- '
## slopes
m_envy ~ b21*unfair
cb ~ b32*m_envy

## (residual) variances
unfair ~~ p11*unfair
m_envy ~~ p22*m_envy
cb  ~~ p33*cb


######## model constraints:

## exogengous predictor, constrain variance to 1
p11 == 1

## residual variance is a function of variance explained by "unfair"
p22 == 1 - b21*p11*b21

## residual variance is a function of variance explained by "m_envy", some of which is explained by "unfair"
p33 == 1 - b32*p22*b32 - b32*b21*p11*b21*b32

'


If you also fit a partial-mediation model, where unfair also has a direct effect on cb (e.g., labeled "b31"), then you need to take into account both sources of explained variance (i.e., also subtract b31*p11*b31).

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
